title: The Ocean's Heat
objective: After this level you can explain how the ocean stores heat.
summary: A thin skin of ocean holds as much heat as the whole atmosphere. The ocean has soaked up about 91% of the extra heat, and marine heatwaves have doubled.

cards.headline: The top few meters of the ocean hold as much heat as Earth's entire atmosphere.
cards.body: Picture all the air above you, right up to space. A thin skin of seawater stores the same amount of heat. That makes the ocean the planet's biggest heat battery.

cards.headline: Slow to warm, slow to cool
cards.body: Water can absorb a lot of heat without its temperature rising much, and it is slower to heat up and cool down than air or land. You've felt this at the beach: at noon the sand scorches your feet while the sea still feels cool. The water has taken in just as much sunshine. It simply hides it better.

cards.fact: The ocean has taken up about 91% of the extra heat trapped in the climate system.
cards.context: That's the IPCC's 2021 figure, and the atmosphere, where we live, got only about 1%. It's virtually certain the upper ocean, down to 700 m, has warmed since the 1970s, and extremely likely that people are the main driver. The warming you feel in the air is the small change; the sea is carrying most of the bill.

cards.headline: Heatwaves under the waves
cards.body: Store that much heat and the sea gets hot spells of its own. Marine heatwaves are spells of persistent, unusually warm sea temperatures, and the IPCC reports with high confidence that they have roughly doubled in frequency since the 1980s. The battery isn't just big. It's charging.
